newsitem.title: BELGIUM: ACEA sees four pct rise in '96 W. Europe car sales.
newsitem.headline: ACEA sees four pct rise in '96 W. Europe car sales.

text.p: New passenger car registrations in western Europe are expected to grow by over four percent in 1996, a spokesman at the European car manufacturers association, ACEA, said on Tuesday.
"We expect growth to be over four percent this year," said James Rosenstein, director of communications at ACEA, adding that this represented a small upward revision from earlier forecasts.
ACEA published figures late on Monday showing that new passenger car registrations in Western Europe rose 12.2 percent to 971,600 in September year-on-year.
In the period January to September, registrations rose 6.7 percent to 10,052,200 from the same period a year earlier.
However, Rosenstein said the strong growth in September was partly the result of soaring sales in France due to the phasing out of a tax rebate scheme for new cars.
"We don't think that this kind of growth is going to continue through the end of the year...we don't expect the end of the year to be good (in western Europe)," he told Reuters.
"And next year we don't expect good growth at all," Rosenstein added.
